tagline: queries within queries — the nesting doll of SQL

placementQuiz.explain: CTE syntax: WITH cte_name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT ... FROM cte_name;
Scalar subquery = exactly one row, one column. Used with =, >, <, etc.

blocks.md: A subquery is a query inside another query. Think of it as a nested box: the inner box produces a value (or list of values) that the outer box uses. CTEs are named boxes you can reuse.

items: Scalar subquery: exactly 1 row, 1 column — use with =, >, <, etc.
Row subquery: exactly 1 row, multiple columns — use with row constructors
Table subquery: multiple rows — use with IN, EXISTS, NOT IN, FROM
Correlated subquery: references outer query columns — runs per outer row
CTE: named temporary result — reusable, readable, can be recursive

blocks.label: scalar subquery
blocks.code:
-- Average salary as scalar
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

-- Scalar in SELECT (per row)
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) AS company_avg
FROM employees;

-- Scalar in expression
SELECT 
  name,
  salary - (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) AS diff_from_avg
FROM employees;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Scalar subquery equivalent
df['company_avg'] = df['salary'].mean()
df['diff'] = df['salary'] - df['salary'].mean()

sections.title: Table Subqueries — IN, EXISTS, NOT IN

blocks.label: in / exists / not in
blocks.py-pandas:
# IN
df[df['dept_id'].isin(nyc_depts['id'])]

# EXISTS (merge)
merged = df.merge(orders[['emp_id']].drop_duplicates(), left_on='id', right_on='emp_id', how='inner')

# NOT EXISTS (anti-join)
merged = df.merge(orders[['emp_id']].drop_duplicates(), left_on='id', right_on='emp_id', how='left', indicator=True)
result = merged[merged['_merge'] == 'left_only']

blocks.md: **NOT IN + subquery with NULL = zero rows.** If subquery returns any NULL, entire NOT IN evaluates to UNKNOWN. Always use NOT EXISTS or filter NULLs: `NOT IN (SELECT ... WHERE col IS NOT NULL)`.

blocks.label: subquery in FROM (derived table)
blocks.code:
-- Derived table in FROM
SELECT dept_id, avg_sal
FROM (
  SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal
  FROM employees
  GROUP BY dept_id
) dept_avg
WHERE avg_sal > 50000;

-- Lateral join (PG) - subquery references outer columns
SELECT e.name, latest.order_date
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT order_date FROM orders o
  WHERE o.emp_id = e.id
  ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1
) latest ON true;
blocks.pg: -- LATERAL allows subquery to reference columns from preceding FROM items

items.q: NOT IN (subquery) with NULL in subquery returns:
items.explain: NOT IN with NULL → UNKNOWN for all rows → zero rows. Use NOT EXISTS instead.

items.q: EXISTS vs IN for 'has orders' query:
options: EXISTS stops at first match; IN may scan all
items.explain: EXISTS is semi-join: stops at first match per outer row. IN may scan entire subquery.

blocks.label: basic cte
blocks.code:
-- Single CTE
WITH high_paid AS (
  SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 100000
)
SELECT * FROM high_paid WHERE dept_id = 1;

-- Multiple CTEs
WITH 
  active AS (SELECT * FROM employees WHERE status = 'active'),
  dept_avg AS (SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id)
SELECT a.name, d.avg_sal
FROM active a
JOIN dept_avg d ON a.dept_id = d.dept_id;

-- CTE in subquery
SELECT * FROM (
  WITH cte AS (SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000)
  SELECT * FROM cte
) t WHERE dept_id = 1;
blocks.pg:
-- CTEs are optimization fences (materialized) in PG < 12
-- PG 12+: can inline with NOT MATERIALIZED
blocks.py-pandas:
# CTE equivalent = intermediate variable
high_paid = df[df['salary'] > 100000]
result = high_paid[high_paid['dept_id'] == 1]

blocks.label: recursive cte
blocks.code:
-- Employee hierarchy: find all reports under manager
WITH RECURSIVE org_chart AS (
  -- Anchor: top-level manager
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, 0 AS level
  FROM employees
  WHERE manager_id IS NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- Recursive: find direct reports
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, oc.level + 1
  FROM employees e
  JOIN org_chart oc ON e.manager_id = oc.id
  WHERE oc.level < 10  -- prevent infinite recursion
)
SELECT * FROM org_chart ORDER BY level, name;
blocks.py-pandas:

for _, row in df.iterrows():

nx.descendants(g, root_id)

blocks.md: Recursive CTE = anchor + recursive part. Always include termination condition (level limit or WHERE NOT EXISTS) to prevent infinite loops.

items.explain: CTE = named, reusable, readable, supports recursion. Subquery = inline, single-use.

options: RECURSIVE keyword + anchor + recursive part + termination
items.explain: All four components required: RECURSIVE keyword, anchor query, recursive part (UNION ALL), termination condition.

revisionCard: Subquery types: scalar (1x1), row (1xN), table (MxN) — each with specific operators
Scalar subquery = single value; use with =, >, <, in expressions
Table subquery: IN, EXISTS, NOT IN, NOT EXISTS, FROM
NOT IN + NULL = disaster; use NOT EXISTS instead
CTE: WITH name AS (...) — reusable, readable, recursive capable
Recursive CTE: anchor + UNION ALL + recursive part + termination

glossary.def: Subquery returning exactly one row and one column (single value).
Subquery that references columns from the outer query; executes once per outer row.
Common Table Expression — named temporary result set defined with WITH clause.
CTE with RECURSIVE keyword that references itself to traverse hierarchies.
EXISTS/IN pattern — returns left rows with at least one match; stops at first match.
NOT EXISTS pattern — returns left rows with NO match in right.
